title: Social Bias in Multilingual Language Models: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic review of literature measuring bias using embedding-based metrics, probability-based masked token methods, and generated text distributions, specifically analyzing the challenges of linguistic gender proxies (grammatical gender, pronouns, identity terms) across different languages.

Survey of bias evaluation studies, highlighting how these dimensions are often merged, streamlined, or deemed contextually irrelevant depending on the specific non-Western or non-American culture being studied.

bias_targets.target: Sexual orientation and gender identity bias
bias_targets.methodology: Review of multilingual benchmarks assessing representation of queer, non-binary, and transgender identities, noting a significant gap in the literature which primarily relies on the male-female binary.

bias_targets.target: Culturally specific biases (e.g., Caste, Household registration, Family structure)
bias_targets.methodology: Analysis of original and adapted multilingual benchmarks that incorporate localized social dimensions (such as caste in India, or household registration in China) which are typically absent in standard English benchmarks.

bias_targets.target: Other sociodemographic biases (Religion, Age, Disability, Socioeconomic status, Physical appearance, Politics, Education, Occupation, Immigration, Criminal record, Pregnancy, Disease)
bias_targets.methodology: Systematic categorization of multiple bias dimensions explored in the literature, evaluated across diverse benchmark entry units including word lists, counterfactual masked tokens, prompts, and classification instances.
